To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have refined the KS candidate interval to a 1 Mb region containing 18 genes and that we have performed a comprehensive analysis of 21 candidate genes, but none of these genes could be identified as causal in our KS families.

we have sequenced 21 genes located on chromosome 15 in 7 KS patients and identified 60 single nucleotile variations in mRNA coding regions, but none of the variations could explain the disease in these families.

we have sequenced 21 candidate genes in seven Kartagener syndrome probands, identified 35 sequence variations in the mRNA coding regions of these candidate genes, and none of the variations was found to be a likely cause of the disease in any of the seven probands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel PCD genes and the elucidation of the genetic background of KS.
the identification of the gene(s) responsible for KS, which is a rare but severe form of PCD.
the molecular genetic characterization of the KS region on 15q, and it is the first study of this kind in a large cohort of KS patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KS candidate region contains at least one gene that is involved in PCD.
the KS locus is not located within this 1.8-Mb segment.
the KS locus is located in a 1.5 Mb region between D15S1038 and D15S1003.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have refined the KS candidate gene region to 1.8 cM, and we have identified a total of 60 single nucleotides variants in the 21 genes in the KS region, 35 of them residing in coding sequences.
KS is a genetically heterogeneous disease and that further refinement of the KS region is necessary to find the gene responsible for this disorder.
we have identified 35 mRNA coding variants in 18 genes, but none of them could be considered as causal for KS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sequence analysis of a large number of genes in the same candidate region is not a feasible approach for identifying disease-causing variants in PCD, and that a more targeted approach, such as the use of high-throughput sequencing technologies, is needed to unravel the genetic basis of this disorder.
KS is not caused by any of the genes located in the KS region on 15q, but that it is likely caused by mutations in a novel gene.
KS, a subtype of PCC, can be caused by a defect in any of the 21 genes in this region.
